title: Hard cutover without legacy; this plan migrates itself; migration is a deletable instruction
decision:
1. The v3 runtime does not read v2 plans. The only v2 awareness is a one-line stop message in the plan commands ("v2 plan: migrate first with `packages/task/docs/migration/v2-to-v3.md`"), deleted together with the migration document once the owner's plans are migrated.
2. The migration is a Markdown instruction executable by a weak model (terra, grok 4.6): mechanical steps using only `plan.py` verbs, a field mapping table, a worked example, and a `plan.py check` loop. Old carriers move to `_v2/` inside the plan directory; nothing is converted by code.
3. Sequencing of this plan: P1, P2 and P3.1 execute under the v2 runtime (it still exists). P3.1 writes the migration instruction and switches commands to v3. P3.2 starts by migrating this plan (PLAN1) with that instruction — the dogfood test of the instruction — then executes under v3 and deletes the v2 runtime. P4 runs entirely under v3.
4. Plans in sibling repositories are not migrated by this plan; the owner runs the instruction per plan.
rationale:
- The owner forbids legacy code (B12); a code migrator would be legacy code reading v2.
- Dogfooding on a real, mid-execution plan validates the instruction on the hardest case (open items, decisions, journal) before the owner uses it on four repositories.
- The v2 runtime must survive until P3.1 closes because P1–P3.1 are executed by it.
consequences: P3.2's launch is `/task:plan-run <ID> P3.2` with the new command text; its v2 stop line directs the executor to migrate PLAN1 first, then `plan.py start`.

evidence.note: owner B12; v2 runtime is required to execute P1–P3.1 of this v2-authored plan
